list: The official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden — names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them, cross-checked against Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-19. Counts (42 Shooting Range challenges, 14 drone race locations, 18 meditation spots, 52 areas, 9 gangs, 8 garages, 9 activity types) are PSN's progress targets as PSNProfiles lists them.

sources.name: PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophies & progress targets

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Follow the roadmap in this guide in order: finish the story first, then the stranger strands, then activities and collectibles, and save the long grinds (250 stunts, 100 vehicles, 50 challenges) for the clean-up stage, because they accumulate while you do everything else. Check the tracker here as you go: when it reads 54 of 55, this one is the last step. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up (1 platinum of 55).

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the opening mission Gone Fishing. If it does not pop, replay the mission from the pause menu; without mission replay, only a new playthrough brings it back.
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy almost every player earns — just play the story from the start and follow the on-screen objectives until the mission-complete screen appears. It teaches the basics (movement, driving and the fishing hook that returns later in the fishing challenge), so take your time and learn the controls instead of rushing. If the trophy does not pop, finish the mission anyway and check the mission-replay option before moving far into Chapter 1. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned by finishing Chapter 1. Missed mission trophies inside the chapter are the real risk — replay a mission before the chapter closes if one fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Play every story mission in Chapter 1 in order until the chapter-end screen appears; there is no shortcut and no side content is required for this one. Use Chapter 1 to learn Leonida: grab a car you like, try the fishing and driving basics, and keep an eye out for stranger icons and activities, because the stranger strands and collectibles you start now count toward later trophies. Finish the chapter's missions cleanly rather than skipping cutscenes you might need for context on later story trophies. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the chapter structure of the list.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned by finishing Chapter 2. Replay any Chapter 2 mission that fails to pop before moving on.
trophies.guide: Complete all of Chapter 2's story missions in order. By now the game opens up: new areas, contacts and the money systems (marked bills, laundering, garages) start to matter, so bank your earnings and start the economy trophies early — launder marked bills through your contacts and buy a garage when you can afford one, because both totals build slowly across the whole game. Keep doing stranger missions as their icons appear; several stranger strands run through multiple chapters. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned by finishing Chapter 3. Replay any Chapter 3 mission that fails to pop before moving on.
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3 — this is the Vice City stretch, and the chapter trophy pops at its end. Mid-game is the best time to start the long counters alongside the story: stunt jumps and near-misses build toward 250 stunts, new vehicles you drive count toward 100 discovered, and every area you drive through counts toward exploring all of Leonida. Do not leave all the collectibles (cards, meditation spots, WAiNK locations) for after the story; picking them up as you pass them saves a long clean-up. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned by finishing Chapter 4. Replay any Chapter 4 mission that fails to pop before the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete all of Chapter 4's story missions. This is the last full chapter before the finale, so before you start the final mission, pause and clear the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) and any stranger strand that is still open — partner availability and stranger missions can dry up once the story ends. Stock up on ammo, armour and a fast getaway car, because the finale and the bank-vault robberies that follow both reward preparation. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: there is exactly one final mission per playthrough. Do the partner and stranger clean-up first (see the roadmap), because the post-story world may not bring those chances back.
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission to earn this gold trophy — it pops at the mission-complete screen, and the platinum is still a long way off, because the 100% completion gold (A Long Road) needs everything else too. Before you start it, work through the roadmap's pre-finale checklist: partner trophies, stranger finales and any story-adjacent secret (the Ocean Beach cocktail, the showroom smash, the bowling alley) that may only be available while the story is live. After the finale, free roam continues, so the collectible and grind trophies can all be finished afterwards. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the gold grade.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission Breakfast Run. Replay the mission from the pause menu if it fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Play the story mission Breakfast Run to its end and follow its objectives — the trophy is tied to finishing this one mission, not to any optional objective, so a normal completion is enough. It is an early mission, so use it to practise driving and partner mechanics: later partner trophies (losing a 4-star wanted level together, robbing three shops in a row) reuse the same co-op movement and getaway skills. If the mission fails, retry it immediately; a failed attempt costs nothing but time. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission The Cartel Heist. Replay the mission from the pause menu if it fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist — a big set-piece robbery, so go in prepared: full ammo, armour, and a fast car parked for the getaway before the mission starts, because heist missions punish a slow escape more than a slow entry. Follow the plan the game lays out rather than improvising; the trophy only needs a completion, and the flashy optional objectives can wait for a replay. The marked bills you earn here feed the laundering trophy (Dime on the Dollar), so launder them through your contacts afterwards instead of sitting on them. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission Child's Play. Replay the mission from the pause menu if it fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Play the story mission Child's Play through to its end. The mission name suggests a family thread in the story, so expect dialogue and choices that set up later missions — pay attention to who you meet, because stranger strands often open from characters introduced in story missions like this one. A normal completion earns the trophy; if it does not pop, use mission replay before you move several missions past it. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission Headliners. Replay the mission from the pause menu if it fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The title points to a high-profile, public-facing job, so expect crowds, attention and a wanted level on the way out — plan your exit route before the loud part starts and keep a fast vehicle nearby. As with every named story mission, the trophy needs only a completion, so finish it first and chase optional objectives on a replay if you want them. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission VCIA Takedown at the airport. The airport secret (Catch Me If You Can) is nearby — read that trophy's guide before you leave VCIA.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown at Vice City International Airport. Because you are already at the airport, read the guide for Catch Me If You Can before you leave — that secret trophy is about an unscheduled departure from VCIA, and the same visit is the natural moment to attempt it. For the mission itself, expect tight airport security and a vehicle-based escape; a normal completion earns the trophy. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missableReason: Story beat: it can only be earned while playing the mission Operation Savage Glory. Replay the mission from the pause menu if it fails to pop.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory — the name suggests a large, chaotic operation, so treat it like a heist: stock ammo and armour beforehand, use cover, and keep your escape vehicle in mind from the start. It is one of the later named story missions, so by now you should have the combat tools (including Combat Focus, which the Gunslinger trophy needs) well practised. A normal completion earns the trophy. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the mission name comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist (pause menu / stats screen) — this is the second gold trophy and the real platinum gate, because 100% means the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles, the activities and the challenges are all done. It cannot be rushed: work through this guide's roadmap in order and tick each trophy off here, and the completion percentage climbs with you. The common last items are the long counters (250 stunts, 50 challenges, all areas explored) and one missed stranger strand, so check your in-game stats against this tracker before declaring yourself done. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the gold grade and the 100% target.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Perform 250 stunts in total — jumps, airtime, near-misses, drifts and other driving feats the game counts as a stunt. The counter is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so the efficient way is to stunt constantly while travelling: take jumps at speed, thread traffic for near-misses, and use fast cars and bikes on open roads. Dedicated stunt spots (ramps and jumps around Leonida) give the fastest rate late in the game, but do not grind all 250 in one sitting early on — let the total build naturally through the story and finish the remainder in the clean-up stage. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 250 target.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity the game offers at least once — PSN tracks 9 activity types. The ones the trophy list itself names are fishing, the arcade, the Shooting Range, drone races, races, bowling and meditation, plus the remaining activities shown in the game's Activities menu. Open that menu, work down it one by one, and tick each off here as you go; you only need to try each type, not win or master it, so a single attempt at each is enough. Do this in the mid-game, while the story is still giving you reasons to visit new places. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 9-type progress target.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges (PSN's count) — the hardest skill trophy on the list. Go to a Shooting Range, pick a challenge, and learn its par time and target pattern before chasing gold; restart a challenge freely, because retries cost nothing and each gold is banked the moment you earn it. Use the best weapon the challenge allows, aim for the head and centre targets first, and reload during movement rather than standing still. Work through the weapon classes one at a time instead of jumping around, and save this for after the story, when your shooting stats and weapon collection are at their best. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 42-challenge count.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations (PSN's count). Each location is its own course, so fly it once slowly to learn the gates and the tight corners, then race it properly — cutting a gate or clipping a wall costs more time than a clean line saves. Drones handle differently from cars: brake before turns, not in them, and keep the throttle steady through gate sequences. The race icons appear on the map as you explore, so clear them region by region while you are doing the exploration trophy. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 14-location count.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word different matters: winning the same race 20 times does not count, so you need 20 separate race events. Race icons appear across Leonida as you explore; vary the vehicle class and the location, and tick each win off in the tracker so you do not repeat one by accident. Pick races that suit your vehicle, learn the first two corners (most races are won or lost there), and use slipstreaming on straights. Street races also build your driving skill, which helps the stunt and getaway trophies. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 20-race target.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head fishing contest, not free fishing. Find Cal and accept his challenge, then fish the way the game taught you in Gone Fishing: cast to the ripples, wait for the bite, and reel with steady tension, easing off when the line strains so it does not snap. Bigger fish score more, so aim for the deeper water and the larger shadows rather than reeling in every small bite. If you lose, challenge him again; the trophy only needs one win. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the fishing basics come from the opening mission the description names.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one full arcade game — walk up to an arcade cabinet, start a game, and play it to its end (or its game-over screen after a full run), rather than just starting it and walking away. Arcade cabinets are found in arcades and bars around Leonida; pick a game you understand quickly, learn its controls in the first minute, and finish the run. This is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so do it while you are clearing that trophy. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableReason: Stranger finale: it can only be earned by finishing Andy's whole mission strand. Once the strand ends it cannot be replayed in the same playthrough, so keep doing Andy's missions whenever his icon appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands work the same way for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone: a character appears on the map, you do their missions one by one as new icons appear, and the trophy pops at the last mission of the strand. Do Andy's missions as soon as they appear instead of letting them pile up — strands can span chapters, and a strand left half-finished at the finale is the most common reason the 100% trophy stalls. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableReason: Stranger finale: it can only be earned by finishing Kenton's whole mission strand. Once the strand ends it cannot be replayed in the same playthrough, so keep doing Kenton's missions whenever his icon appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand — the title hints at boats, so expect water, docks and a getaway by sea somewhere in the strand. As with every stranger finale, the work is the strand itself: follow Kenton's icon each time it appears, finish each mission, and the trophy pops at the last one. If Kenton's icon has not appeared in a while, move the story forward a mission or two; strands often unlock with story progress. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableReason: Stranger finale: it can only be earned by finishing Billy's whole mission strand. Once the strand ends it cannot be replayed in the same playthrough, so keep doing Billy's missions whenever his icon appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand — the name points to a lone biker, so expect motorcycle riding and open-road missions in this strand. Keep a fast bike handy for Billy's missions, follow his icon whenever it appears on the map, and finish the strand before the story finale if you can. The trophy pops at the last mission, not at the first meeting. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The five named stranger finales in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of the eight, so you need three more strands from the other strangers marked on the map. Stranger icons appear as you explore and as the story advances — check the map after every story mission for new icons, drive to each one, and finish the strand before starting the next story beat. Count your finished strands in this tracker: when it reads 8, the silver pops. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 8-strand target.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableReason: Stranger finale: it can only be earned by finishing Randy's whole mission strand. Once the strand ends it cannot be replayed in the same playthrough, so keep doing Randy's missions whenever his icon appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand — the title points to supply runs, so expect delivery and pick-up missions, likely with a vehicle full of goods and a time limit or pursuers. Do Randy's missions promptly when his icon appears, keep a sturdy vehicle ready for the supply runs, and finish the strand before the finale. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableReason: Stranger finale: it can only be earned by finishing Tyrone's whole mission strand. Once the strand ends it cannot be replayed in the same playthrough, so keep doing Tyrone's missions whenever his icon appears.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand — the title suggests music, spinning records or a DJ thread, so expect nightlife venues and a sound-system flavour to his missions. Follow Tyrone's icon whenever it appears, finish each mission in the strand, and the trophy pops at the last one. Like the other stranger finales, it counts as one of the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida (PSN's count). Meditation spots are scenic, quiet places — viewpoints, beaches, hilltops and parks — marked when you get close or shown on the map once discovered. Visit them region by region while you are exploring for The Goodtime State, sit and meditate at each one, and tick it off here so you do not revisit the same spot twice. None of them is story-locked, so any spot you miss can be visited in free roam after the finale. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 18-spot count.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableReason: One unique animal: if it escapes or is killed the wrong way, it may not return in the same playthrough. Prepare before you start the hunt and save first if the game lets you.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a single, specific animal, not just any wildlife. Find Bret, take the hunt, and follow his clues or the trail markers to the animal's territory. Go prepared: a scoped rifle, quiet approach, and patience — spook the animal and the hunt may be over. Take the shot only when you have a clear, close one, and collect the animal afterwards to complete Bret's request. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets — find the cards scattered across Leonida and fill three sets in your collection. Cards are found in shops, houses, vehicles and out-of-the-way spots; check the collection screen to see which sets are closest to complete and hunt the missing cards first. A set only counts when every card in it is collected, so a half-finished set earns nothing — prioritise the set with the fewest cards missing. Cards are not story-locked, so any card can be picked up in free roam after the finale. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 3-set target.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It — the in-game photo-sharing app — at 100 different locations. Each location only counts once, so the method is to WAiNK everywhere you go: viewpoints, landmarks, businesses, beaches and street corners, one snap per place. The fastest route is to combine it with the exploration trophy: every time you enter a new area for The Goodtime State, WAiNK it before you leave. The counter is cumulative across the whole game, so start early and it finishes itself during the clean-up stage. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 100-location target.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges from the game's challenge list — the mixed bag of driving, combat, exploration and activity feats the game tracks under Challenges. Open the challenge list, pick the easiest unfinished ones first (short drives, simple stunts, low-count goals), and work through them in batches between story missions. Challenges overlap heavily with other trophies — stunts count toward 250, races toward 20 wins, exploration toward all areas — so a lot of the 50 will complete themselves while you chase the rest of the list. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 50-challenge target.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableReason: Needs your partner beside you — partner missions end as the story moves on, so attempt this while partner missions are available, before the finale.
trophies.guide: With your partner with you, raise your wanted level to 4 stars, then lose the police and escape. Get to 4 stars somewhere with cover nearby (a parking garage, tunnels, or the countryside), then break line of sight, switch to a fast car or go on foot into alleys, and stay hidden until the stars blink and clear. Do not fight the police at 4 stars — escaping is the goal, and your partner must survive with you. Attempt it during a partner mission or free-roam stretch while your partner is available, not after the story has moved on. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableReason: Needs your partner beside you and three shops in a row without the wanted level dropping — partner availability ends as the story moves on, so do it while partner missions are available.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back-to-back without losing your wanted level — the trick is the middle word: you must keep at least some wanted level alive through all three robberies, so do not hide long enough for the stars to clear between shops. Plan a route first: pick three shops close together, rob the first, drive straight to the second while the police are still looking, then the third, and only then escape. Keep the robberies quick, keep your partner close, and use a fast car parked outside each shop. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive or enter 100 distinct vehicle models, and each new model is logged. The counter rewards variety, not volume: driving the same sedan 100 times counts once. Vary everything you drive: cars, bikes, trucks, boats, aircraft and the odd special vehicle you find parked in unusual places. Car parks, docks, the airport and wealthy neighbourhoods are the best hunting grounds, and every story mission with a new vehicle is free progress. Check the vehicle log to see what you still miss. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 100-vehicle target.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode. Wait for a fight with at least five enemies grouped together, let your Combat Focus meter fill, then trigger it and work fast: headshots, one target after another, without letting the meter run out. The easiest setups are missions or police chases where enemies cluster in a doorway or street; do not waste it on two or three scattered targets. If you only get four, the attempt fails — reload the checkpoint or find a bigger group and try again. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableReason: A one-time airport moment: an unscheduled departure from VCIA may only be possible on the visit when the chance presents itself. Attempt it during the VCIA Takedown mission visit, before you leave the airport.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — get to VCIA, find an aircraft (or a vehicle on the runway side), and leave the airport by air or at speed without going through the normal departure. The natural moment is your VCIA Takedown mission visit: read this guide before that mission, and attempt the departure while you are already inside the airport. Expect airport security and a wanted level, so have a plan for the runway and the take-off, and do not stop to fight on the tarmac. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the VCIA connection comes from the VCIA Takedown mission the description names.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the military tanks. Raise your wanted level high in free roam until the military responds, or find a Rhino at a military base or during a story moment that brings tanks out, then get inside one (or survive one) and use it: drive it, fire its cannon, and cause chaos until the trophy pops. Tanks are slow but nearly unstoppable, so the risk is not the tank, it is getting to it — approach with armour, a fast vehicle and a clear route, and expect a 4- or 5-star response once you are rolling. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery, not a smash-and-grab. Go at a quiet time, enter calmly, avoid the cameras and the guards' sightlines, take the jewelry, and leave before any alarm sounds. If a guard spots you or the alarm trips, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting it out. A suppressed weapon and a fast getaway car parked outside help, but patience is the real tool: watch the guard patrols for one full cycle before you move. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault is its own job: case the bank, get inside the vault, grab the cash, and — the part the trophy names — escape, because a robbery that ends in a bust or a death does not count. Plan the escape before the entry: a fast car or bike parked close, a route away from the main roads, and a place to break line of sight. Vaults are found across Leonida, so clear them region by region during the clean-up stage, and do the Cartel Heist-style preparation (ammo, armour) for the tougher ones. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 5-vault target.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — the classic GTA blitz. Find an armored truck on its route (they run the main roads and highways), stop it by blocking the road or disabling it, breach the back, take the cash, and escape before the police box you in. The escape is the hard half: have a getaway car ready, do not linger at the truck once the money is yours, and break line of sight quickly. Armored trucks keep appearing in free roam, so a failed attempt just means finding the next one. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida (PSN's count) — visit every named area on the map, from Vice City and Ocean Beach to the swamps, the Keys and the northern countryside. The map tracks which areas you have visited, so open it and look for the blank patches: drive, fly or sail to each one and stay until the area name appears. Combine this with the other exploration trophies (WAiNK a photo in each new area, meditate at spots you pass, discover new vehicles) so one trip earns several counters at once. Nothing is story-locked, so finish it in free roam after the finale. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 52-area count.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs (PSN's count) — one operation per gang. Illegal operations are the gangs' off-the-books businesses (stash houses, labs, warehouses); find them by exploring gang territory, following tips and stranger leads, and watching for the operation markers. Each gang's operation is a small raid: get in, take the goods or cash, and get out before reinforcements arrive. Tick each gang off in this tracker as you clear its operation, because the trophy only pops when all 9 are done. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 9-gang count.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableReason: A specific place and moment: a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. It may only be available while the story brings you there, so do it the first time you are on Ocean Beach with the chance — do not assume it waits forever.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — go to a bar or venue on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take in the view. The trophy's title (a nod to the very first GTA moment) suggests this is a quiet, scripted beat rather than a grind, so look for the prompt when you are at the beachfront: sit, order, and let the scene play. If no prompt appears, try the beachfront bars at different times of day and after story progress, because the moment may be tied to a story visit. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the Ocean Beach location comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableReason: A specific showroom moment: smashing out of a vehicle showroom in classic style may only be possible during the story visit that brings you there. Attempt it the first time you are inside a showroom with a vehicle.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — the callback to the original GTA showroom escape. Get inside a vehicle showroom with a car, then drive it straight out through the glass frontage instead of using the door. Pick a fast car, aim for the biggest window, and keep accelerating through the glass and out onto the street; the trophy is about the exit, so do not stop to admire the damage. If a story mission takes you into a showroom, attempt it there first, because that visit may be your only scripted chance. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.missableReason: A specific venue moment: the follow-through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley may be tied to a story or stranger visit. Play a full game there the first time you visit, rather than leaving it for later.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — go to that bowling alley, start a game, and play it through to the end, following through on your throws. Bowling is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so this trophy and that one can be earned in the same visit. Take your time with the aim and power: a straight, steady throw beats a wild one, and a full game is only a few frames. If the alley visit comes from a story or stranger mission, play the game while you are there. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; the venue comes from the description itself.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableReason: A partnership moment: it depends on your partner and the story's partnership arc, which ends with the story. Build the partnership while the story is live; it may not be available after the finale.
trophies.guide: Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal — a beat in the game's partnership story where you and your partner do something that catches the public eye. Play the partner missions, keep your partner close in free roam, and follow the partnership thread the story offers: the trophy is about the relationship, not a single button press, so it comes from progressing the partnership rather than from a grind. If a partner mission offers a public or showy option, take it. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableReason: Choices cannot be unmade: the trophy tracks choices you make through the story, and a choice skipped or made the other way may not come back in the same playthrough. PSN tracks a progress count of 500 for this one — make choices whenever the game offers them.
trophies.guide: Make choices — the trophy tracks the decisions you make across the game (PSN lists a progress target of 500 choices), and it pops when the count is met. The method is simple: whenever the game offers a choice, in dialogue, in a mission approach, or in the open world, make one instead of walking away. Small choices count alongside big story ones, so the total builds all game long. Because choices cannot be unmade, do not leave choice moments for later — take them when they appear. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 500-choice progress target.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableReason: A second-try moment: it is about succeeding on the second attempt at something that failed the first time. If you succeed first try everywhere, the chance may never come — so when an attempt fails, retry it immediately instead of reloading an old save.
trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try — the trophy is about a second attempt that works after a first attempt failed. The practical advice is about how you play, not where: when a mission, challenge or attempt fails, retry it right away from the retry prompt instead of reloading an older save, because the retry is the second try the trophy counts. Do not engineer failures on purpose everywhere — play normally, and when a genuine failure happens, take the retry. If it has not popped by the late game, it is worth failing and retrying a repeatable challenge once, deliberately. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableReason: A strange, possibly random event: it may only trigger once, at a specific place or time. Explore odd places (remote spots, strange landmarks) at night and follow anything unusual you see.
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the trophy is for a weird, out-of-the-ordinary event in Leonida, the kind of thing that makes you ask what just happened. Explore the odd corners of the map: remote swamp clearings, strange landmarks, deserted stretches of road, especially at night, and investigate anything unusual (lights, sounds, odd characters) instead of driving past. These events are often random or time-based, so patience and exploration matter more than a checklist — keep exploring during the clean-up stage and it will find you. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle and knock the target down like a bowling pin. Drive slowly past a pedestrian (or an enemy in a light combat spot), swing the melee weapon from the vehicle window, and connect cleanly. Speed is the enemy here: too fast and you miss, too slow and it is not a drive-by — a slow cruise is the sweet spot. It can be attempted any time in free roam, so there is no missable risk; practise on a quiet street and it pops quickly. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the list's make-up.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from heists and robberies (the Cartel Heist, bank vaults, armored trucks), and they are only worth their clean value once laundered — so after every big job, visit your contacts and launder the take instead of letting it sit. The total is cumulative: $250,000 of laundered money, not $250,000 held at once, so steady laundering after every job gets there without a single huge score. Start early, because the heist money dries up late in the game. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the $250,000 target.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, ammo, food, vehicle mods and anything else the shops of Leonida sell. The total is cumulative across every shop, so it builds naturally as you gear up for missions; the efficient path is to spend on things you actually use (weapons and ammo for the Shooting Range golds, armour for the heists, vehicle upgrades for races) rather than buying junk for the sake of it. Check your spending total in the stats screen if you want to know how far along you are, and finish the remainder in the clean-up stage with a shopping trip. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the $100,000 target.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties (PSN's count) — the garages for sale across Leonida. Garages cost money, so save through the mid-game and buy them as you can afford them; each one also gives you storage for the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good, so the two trophies help each other. Check the property listings on the in-game property site or the for-sale signs, buy the cheapest ones first, and keep the expensive ones for the clean-up stage when your laundered heist money is in. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 8-garage count.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game vehicle-sharing app. Find a vehicle, open the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone, and register it; each distinct vehicle counts once, so register ten different ones rather than the same car ten times. Scooters and small vehicles are the easiest to find (the app's name is the hint), but any vehicle the app accepts counts. Do it while you are discovering vehicles for Whip It Good, so one drive earns both counters. Sources: the official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the 10-vehicle target.
